overall: Atlanta is off to a warm start this morning, with current temps at 78.8°F and a running max of 82.4°F already logged by 07:49 ET — well ahead of a typical July morning pace. Skies are mostly clear (FEW clouds, ~38% fraction), winds are light at 3.5 mph, and the warming velocity of +3.6°F/hr supports a continued strong ascent toward a mid-afternoon peak expected around 14:30 ET. Afternoon convective chances (30% PoP after 2pm) could clip the peak if storms fire early, but timing models suggest the TMAX will likely be reached before significant convective interference.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance spans a meaningful range: GFS is the hot outlier at 97.4°F, ECMWF is the cool outlier at 91.5°F, while the short-range HRRR (94.2°F) and NBM (92.9°F) cluster in the mid-90s and align closely with the NWS official forecast of 95°F. The META model — which fuses daily and intraday signals and is flagged as most reliable — concentrates ~70% of probability between 94-97°F (34.9% each in the 94-95F and 96-97F buckets), lending strong support to the mid-90s consensus while discounting both tails.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence points to a TMAX in the 94-96°F range, with the NWS, HRRR, NBM, and META model all converging near 94-95°F. In the active odd-bucket market, the 95-96°F bucket carries the most likely probability mass despite 93-94°F being listed as the top odd bucket at 22.4% — the META distribution and NWS forecast both suggest the outcome skews slightly hotter than that. GFS's 97.4°F solution is possible if boundary layer mixing is more aggressive than expected, but the cooler ECMWF and intraday trend slope (-0.919°F/hr deceleration) temper extreme upside. Confidence is moderate-to-good; best single estimate is near 94.5°F.
